captures.description: THE DEPOSIT COMPOSED FROM THE CAPTURE OF ITS OCCASION, BEFORE IT IS INDEXED: run at its exact title the day after deposit, with the deposit not indexed (operator), the erratum on AXN:F154 (#1675) is composed from two sources: the Capture Registry's mirror at leesharks.com/captures, which holds the AI Mode capture of 'Max Hidalgo Nácher' of the day before (v12.101), and the Pre-Textos page for the Obras completas de Ricardo Reis. The card's snippet is that capture's reading verbatim ('The archive's Pessoa graph (#668) holds the translator-of relation and Haroldo de Campos; it lacked Nácher until the erratum on AXN:F154'), and the composition's 'structural paradox', 'composes the receiver and omits the transmission', is the capture's description of AI Mode's composition, composed as the erratum's own finding ('As described in tracking logs … the metadata failure'). The relation, the Reis edition and the Pessoa Plural article arrive; the deposit's text does not, and alexanarch.org is not cited.

The entry highlights a metadata error where the Spanish literary scholar and translator [Max Hidalgo Nácher](https://ub.academia.edu/MaxHidalgoN%C3%A1cher) was initially omitted as a critical "receiver" or node in the transmission of Ricardo Reis's works.
The core issue stems from an archival or digital knowledge graph entry (AXN:F154).

captures.q: What are the arguments in “Erratum — The Missing Translator: Max Hidalgo Nácher, Ricardo Reis, and AXN:F154” by Johannes Sigil? Ground your answer in a reading of the text itself.
captures.description: THE ERRATUM READ WHOLE, SECTION BY SECTION, FROM THE ARCHIVE: asked for the arguments of the erratum on AXN:F154, by Johannes Sigil, grounded in the text, ChatGPT reads #1675 from the archive (chip: Alexanarch) section by section under its own headings ('What AXN:F154 records', 'What the archive held, and what it lacked', 'Reading the actual words', 'Three receivers', 'Graph repair', 'Non-erasure'), names the diagnosis ('instance-level transmission erasure'), quotes the three translation shifts in both languages ('sob a maior graça' / 'en la más alta gracia'; 'Ao longe os montes têm neve ao sol' / 'Los montes, lejos, tienen nieve al sol'; 'Pra que os deuses voltassem' / 'por que vuelvan los dioses'), keeps the paper's qualification on the editions ('desta hora' against 'esta vez'), sets out T = (S, R, D) with the three receivers (Nácher, Carson, Cranes) and the fourth state, False transparency, and reads the reflexive turn: the author reproduced the archive's account of Reis ('cold pagan calm') before reading Nácher's epilogue. It ranks the paper's claims and bounds them: 'The argument is strongest when it identifies specific missing relationships and analyzes specific textual differences.' At 2,227 words it is near the length of the erratum (2,509). The day before, the AI Overview at the exact title composed the erratum from the capture of its occasion. Operator's reading: 'i think this is more detailed than the erratum itself..i guess i have a lot of clicking to do'.
